analysis:
The PR adds a `publish_revision_only` input to .github/workflows/register-model.yml. In that mode the workflow sends only {version, hugging_face_artifact} to POST /v1/admin/models/<url-encoded model_id>/publish-revision. The existing Bearer MODEL_REGISTRY_PUBLISHING_KEY is reused. Other changes are a changelog entry and docs/developer/test.md describing the workflow tests.

Checked and found no concrete regression:
- Inputs reach shell and jq only through env vars and --arg/--argjson, so there is no expression injection.
- model_id is percent-encoded with safe="", so slashes cannot alter the route.
- The key is not logged and is sent only to the coordinator_url input. That behavior is unchanged and is a pre-existing property of the dispatcher.
- The backend handler is out of scope and not visible here. Whether it authorizes the key, checks the revision is immutable and uploaded, and enforces any weight-hash check is unverified. Weight integrity (A-004, T-012, T-027) and the fail-open weight-hash gap (SEC-007, TB-002) therefore depend on that platform-owned endpoint.

Minor observations, not filed as findings:
- The `promote` input is ignored in revision-only mode, which always promotes.
- A model_id of `..` could be dot-segment-normalized by curl.
- Both are limited to a dispatcher who already holds workflow-dispatch rights.

The docs reference scripts/test_model_registry_workflow.py, scripts/test_publish_model_revision.py and docs/operations/model-revisions.md. These are not in the supplied diff, so I could not verify they exist or what they test. No threat-model update is required for the provider scope.
